history.caption: A model’s published score hinges on two unowned conversion joints outside the model, shown here as an unseated inspection latch and an open verification cover on a control-room workbench.
history.title: Eval pipeline renderer parser gate clay assembly

style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: Matte clay render of a small mechanical eval pipeline assembly resting on a weathered concrete control-room workbench before a blurred data hall rack row. Three recognisable engineered parts in deliberate arrangement: a central graphite model module with cooling fins seated in a brushed aluminium rail, an input-side renderer inspection gate with an optical glass readback head, and an output-side parser snap-latch connector with cover unlatched and a visible gap where the sensor head does not fully seat. One hard raking key light from the left throws long contact shadows over moulding seams; palette graphite, bone white, safety yellow. Extreme asymmetry, assembly on left third, generous negative space to the right; no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, labels, engravings
rationale: The story is structural and abstract: two unowned joints outside the model determine the score, but there is no literal facility to photograph. A matte clay mechanical assembly makes the renderer and parser tangible as inspection gates with a visible gap and open cover, avoiding the sterile datacenter trope while giving the failure a tactile, mechanistic truth.
subject: A small mechanical eval pipeline assembly with a central model module flanked by renderer and parser inspection gates, one unseated and one open.
core_thesis: An eval score is made twice outside the model—once when a renderer turns the run into the text a judge reads and once when a parser turns the reply into a verdict—and because both fail quietly at exactly the inputs where the model is weakest, a score is only worth trusting when the pipeline reports what it rendered, what it parsed and how often the fallback fired.
core_conflict: Two unowned external conversion steps—renderer and parser—silently add or drop points on the same stored outputs, while the model in the middle remains the only part anyone measures.
composition: Extreme asymmetry, assembly on left third, generous negative space to the right
alt_text: Two matte clay modules meet on a cracked concrete floor, a yellow connector latch hanging open between them, in a dim server room.

review.reason: The depicted object is literally a compact pipeline assembly with a central module flanked by two inspection gates, one of which is visibly open/unseated, matching the article's rendered-parsed eval pipeline mechanism rather than a different industry or generic filler.
